Lessons.Title: Fractional Measurements on Line Plots
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: You will organize and interpret fractional measurement data on a line plot.
Key idea: Fractional measurements are recorded with a uniform ruler scale and displayed by a line plot whose marks represent observations.
How to reason: Check quarter- or eighth-inch units, preserve repeated marks on the plot, then answer measurement questions by exact fractional arithmetic.
Source-inspired opening: Warm-up: Notice and Wonder: Which Ruler? 	 (10 minutes). Use the teacher-provided mathematical representations and explain how different valid answers arise.

Activity 1:  Measure to the Nearest $\frac{1}{4}$ and $\frac{1}{8}$ Inch	 [OPTIONAL] (25 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(\frac{1}{4}\), \(\frac{1}{8}\). First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.

Activity 2:  Colored-pencil Measurements	 (20 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(\frac{1}{4}\), \(1\frac{3}{4}\), \(2\frac{1}{4}\), \(5\frac{1}{4}\). First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.

Activity 3: Noah's Colored Pencils (15 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(\frac{1}{2}\), \(6\frac{1}{4}\), \(1\frac{3}{4}\), The three longest pencils are exactly 5 inches longer than the shortest one.. First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.
